title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Catastro - CadastralParcel
description: Basic unit of territorial division in the Spanish Cadastre: a plot of land delimited geographically, which may contain one or more cadastral properties (edintcat:CadastralParcel, subclass of geosparql:Feature).

id.description: Property. Unique identifier of the entity

type.description: Property. NGSI-LD Entity type. It must be equal to 'CadastralParcel'

dateCreated.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/DateTime'. Entity creation timestamp. This will usually be allocated by the storage platform.

dateModified.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/DateTime'. Timestamp of the last modification of the entity. This will usually be allocated by the storage platform.

name.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/name'. Name of this item.

alternateName.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/alternateName'. An alternative name for this item.

description.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/description'. Description of this item.

source.description: Property. A sequence of characters giving the source of the entity data.

dataProvider.description: Property. A sequence of characters identifying the provider of the harmonised data entity.

seeAlso.description: Property. Model:'https://schema.org/URL'. list of uri pointing to additional resources about the item.

hasCadastralProperty.description: Relationship. The CadastralProperty/properties this parcel contains, e.g. flats in a horizontal division (edintcat:hasCadastralProperty).

hasClass.description: Property. Classification (urban/rural/special-characteristics) of the parcel, from the Clase controlled vocabulary (edintcat:hasClass).

hasAddress.description: Relationship. The parcel's address (edintcat:hasAddress), in the external callejero:Portal vocabulary (not modeled by this candidate).

hasGeometry.description: Relationship. Reference to the parcel's geometry (geosparql:hasGeometry). The source's own real examples represent this indirectly via a separate geo:Geometry resource carrying WKT and area, mirroring how this candidate family already treats large/complex geometries (e.g. edint-zona-regulatoria's RegulatedZone.hasGeometry) rather than inlining a GeoProperty.
